answer: A hardware attestation protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by binding each agent identity to an endorsement relic sealed in secure silicon. Participants submit enclave quotes to an admission summit, relegating uncertified entities to an isolated network tundra. An attacker generating fake agents must acquire discrete physical coprocessors with valid manufacturer keys. However, this system relies on centralized chipmakers and remains vulnerable to microarchitectural side-channel exploits.
